title: Actor reentrancy and stale results
summary: Use a generation check after an await so an older refresh cannot overwrite a newer request’s result.
code: func refresh(_ load: @Sendable () async throws -> String) async throws -> Bool {
guard ticket == generation else { return false }
triggers: Swift actor reentrancy changes state across an await
out-of-order asynchronous responses overwrite newer state
prompts: Refresh a preview as the user changes inputs and let only the latest request update the display.
Pause the first load, finish a second refresh, then prove that the first result cannot replace it.
invariant: Only the latest started refresh can commit. Validation and the write occur in one actor turn without an intervening await.
mantra: Capture before await; revalidate before commit.
pitfalls: Actor isolation protects memory access but does not make the entire async method atomic.
Checking the generation before the suspension would miss refreshes started while the load was running.
This policy discards older results even if the latest request fails. It does not cancel superseded work.
